utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Hi. Come on in. What's on your mind today?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I keep asking myself what's the point. Like really — what's the actual point of working so hard when nothing changes. I feel like I'm going nowhere.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: That existential frustration is very real. What area of your life feels most stuck right now?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: My career mostly. I've been at the same level for three years. I just want it to stop — this cycle of trying and failing. It's exhausting and I'm not sure how much longer I can keep going like this.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: Sustained effort without visible reward is genuinely demoralizing. How has this been affecting your home life?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: I'm more irritable. My partner says I seem checked out. Sometimes I think about if I just disappeared from my life for a month — like ran away — how much better everyone would feel without the constant cloud I bring.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: The idea of escape is very human when we're overwhelmed. What would that break ideally give you?

utterances.speaker: Patient
utterances.text: Just peace. I don't want to hurt myself or anything dramatic like that. I just genuinely wish I could step off the hamster wheel. Nothing matters anymore in my current job. It's just dead end after dead end.

utterances.speaker: Therapist
utterances.text: I hear you. That feeling of meaninglessness at work can bleed into everything. Let's talk about what a realistic reset could look like.
